subject: Culture
title: Viking Ship Burials
description: A quick, practical guide to Viking Ship Burials.

hook.text: In 921 AD, an Arab traveler watched Vikings burn a chieftain on his ship with weapons, food, and a sacrificed slave.

buildup.text: Ibn Fadlan's account is the most detailed record of a Viking funeral. The ceremony lasted ten days.

discovery.text: Ship burials sent the dead to the afterlife with everything they'd need—including servants and animals.

twist.text: The Oseberg ship burial held two women with extraordinary grave goods. Female power existed in Viking death rites.

climax.text: Not every Viking was ship-buried. Most were cremated simply. Ship burials were reserved for the elite few.

punchline.text: Even in death, Vikings traveled in style.

quiz.question: Who wrote the most detailed account of a Viking funeral?
